pages.title: color
pages.description: Color construction and Tea’s standard palette.
pages.intro: Functions and constants in the `color` namespace.

entries.summary: Returns a color with its transparency replaced.
signatures: color color.new(series color color, series int | float transp)

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The base color. Its current transparency is discarded.

entries.returns: The color with the given transparency; `na` when either argument is `na`.
entries.body:
`alpha` is the opacity channel, from 0 (invisible) to 255 (opaque), which an emitted color shows as `a`; halves round up. The red, green and blue channels stay the same. A constant `transp` outside 0 to 100 is a compile error; any other value outside that range, such as an input’s, is clamped to it.

**Formula**

$$
\begin{aligned}
c &= \min(\max(\mathit{transp}, 0), 100) \\
\mathit{alpha} &= \operatorname{round}\left(\frac{255 \cdot (100 - c)}{100}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

**Example:** Transparency 80 keeps the red, green and blue channels and sets the opacity `a` to 51 of 255, the `33` at the end of the hex code. Transparency 50 gives 127.5, which rounds up to 128.

```tea
faded = color.new(color.blue, 80)
emit "blue" color.blue
emit "faded" faded
emit "hex" str.tostring(faded)
emit "half" color.new(color.blue, 50)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  blue                              faded                            hex        half
0      {"r":33,"g":150,"b":243,"a":255}  {"r":33,"g":150,"b":243,"a":51}  #2196F333  {"r":33,"g":150,"b":243,"a":128}
```

**See also:** [`color.rgb`](#color.rgb)

entries.summary: Builds a color from red, green and blue components.
signatures:
color color.rgb(
    series int | float red,
    series int | float green,
    series int | float blue,
    series int | float transp = …
)

parameters.name: transp
parameters.description: The transparency, from 0 (opaque, the default) to 100 (invisible), applied as [`color.new`](#color.new) applies it.

entries.returns: The color; `na` when any argument is `na`.
entries.body:
Components are rounded to whole numbers, with halves rounded up. A constant outside its range is a compile error; any other value outside it is clamped.

**Example:** Without `transp` the color is opaque, `a` 255; a transparency of 80 leaves an opacity of 51.

```tea
emit "amber" color.rgb(255, 191, 0)
emit "faded" color.rgb(255, 191, 0, 80)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  amber                            faded
0      {"r":255,"g":191,"b":0,"a":255}  {"r":255,"g":191,"b":0,"a":51}
```

**See also:** [`color.new`](#color.new)

entries.summary: Tea’s standard palette of named colors.
entries.body:
Each constant is a `const color`.

The values belong to Tea, not to the host application’s theme. Use [`color.new`](#color.new) for a transparent version.

**Example:** The close falls only on bar 4, so `bar_color` is `color.red` there and `color.green` elsewhere; on bar 0, `close[1]` is `na` and the comparison is `false`.

```tea
falling = close < close[1]
emit "close" close
emit "bar_color" falling ? color.red : color.green
```

```csv
time,close
0,9
1,12
2,12
3,15
4,12
5,18
```

**Output:**

```text
index  close  bar_color
0      9      {"r":76,"g":175,"b":80,"a":255}
1      12     {"r":76,"g":175,"b":80,"a":255}
2      12     {"r":76,"g":175,"b":80,"a":255}
3      15     {"r":76,"g":175,"b":80,"a":255}
4      12     {"r":255,"g":82,"b":82,"a":255}
5      18     {"r":76,"g":175,"b":80,"a":255}
```

**See also:** [`color.new`](#color.new), [`color.rgb`](#color.rgb)

pages.title: array
pages.description: Functions for ordered, variable-length collections.
pages.intro: See [types](#reference/language/types) for the `array<T>` type and [memory model](#memory-model) for how array values are copied and shared. Unlike Pine Script, where collections are references, a Tea collection is a value: assigning it or passing it to a function copies it, so a function that pushes to its argument leaves the caller’s collection unchanged. Every function whose first parameter is `self` can also be called as a method on the collection: `values.push(x)` is the same call as `array.push(values, x)`.

entries.summary: Creates an array, empty or with a given number of elements.
signatures:
array<T> array.new<T: storable>(
    series int size,
    series T initial = …
)

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of elements. Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: initial
parameters.description: The value of every element. Without it, each element is the element type’s empty value (`na`, or `false` for `bool`).

entries.returns: A new array.
entries.body:
Write the element type in angle brackets, as in `array.new<float>(3)`, unless `initial` gives it. A negative or `na` size stops the run with an error. A collection holds at most 100,000 elements; a larger size also stops the run. Each change copies the collection and counts against a per-bar allocation budget; see [`array.push`](#array.push). A variable declared as `array<float> values = na` holds no array, and calling a function on it stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `zeros` holds three zeros; without `initial`, both elements of `missing` are `na`.

```tea
zeros = array.new(3, 0.0)
missing = array.new<float>(2)
emit "zeros" zeros
emit "missing" missing
```

**Output:**

```text
index  zeros    missing
0      [0,0,0]  ["na","na"]
```

**See also:** [`array.from`](#array.from)

entries.summary: Creates an array holding the given values in order.
entries.returns: A new array.
entries.body:
The element type comes from the values; integers mixed with floats make a `float` array. With no values, or only `na`, write the type: `array.from<float>()`.

**Example:** The `int` values 1 and 4 join 2.5 in one `array<float>`; `first` is the element at position 0.

```tea
levels = array.from(1, 2.5, 4)
emit "levels" levels
emit "first" levels.get(0)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  levels     first
0      [1,2.5,4]  1
```

**See also:** [`array.new`](#array.new)

entries.summary: Returns the number of elements in an array.
entries.returns: The number of elements.

entries.summary: Tests whether an array has no elements.
entries.returns: `true` when the array has no elements.

entries.summary: Returns the element at a position.
signatures: T array.get<T: storable>(series array<T> self, series int index)

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position, counting from 0 for the first element.

entries.returns: The element. A struct element is the same struct, not a copy.
entries.body:
An index that is negative, `na`, or not less than the size stops the run with an error; negative indexes do not count from the end.

**Example:** Positions count from 0, so `values.get(1)` is the second element, 20.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
emit "second" values.get(1)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  second
0      20
```

**See also:** [`array.set`](#array.set)

entries.summary: Returns the first element of an array.
entries.returns: The element at position 0.
entries.body:
An empty array stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `first` is the element at position 0, 10.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
emit "first" values.first()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  first
0      10
```

**See also:** [`array.last`](#array.last)

entries.summary: Returns the last element of an array.
entries.returns: The element at the highest position.
entries.body:
An empty array stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `last` is the element at the highest position, 30.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
emit "last" values.last()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  last
0      30
```

**See also:** [`array.first`](#array.first)

entries.summary: Replaces the element at a position.
signatures:
void array.set<T: storable>(
    series array<T> self,
    series int index,
    series T value
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The array to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position, counting from 0 for the first element.

entries.body:
An index that is negative, `na`, or not less than the size stops the run with an error. Each change copies the collection and counts against a per-bar allocation budget; see [`array.push`](#array.push).

**Example:** `values.set(1, 25)` replaces the second element.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
values.set(1, 25)
emit "values" values
```

**Output:**

```text
index  values
0      [10,25,30]
```

**See also:** [`array.get`](#array.get)

entries.summary: Appends a value to the end of an array.
signatures:
void array.push<T: storable>(
    series array<T> self,
    series T value
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The array to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.body:
Appending to one variable does not change array values already assigned to other variables or committed to history, and a function that pushes to an array it receives changes only its own copy. A struct element is stored by reference. A collection holds at most 100,000 elements; pushing past that stops the run with an error.

Each `push`, like every change to a collection, copies the whole collection into new storage. One bar may allocate at most 10,000 times and 16 MiB in all, where each copy counts 16 bytes plus 8 for each number, bool, string or color it holds; past either limit the run stops with `HEAP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. So an array of numbers created empty in a bar fails on its 2,046th push in that bar.

**Example:** Declared with `var`, the array keeps its elements from bar to bar, so it gains one close on each bar.

```tea
var closes = array.new<float>()
closes.push(close)
emit "close" close
emit "closes" closes
```

```csv
time,close
0,9
1,12
2,12
3,15
4,12
5,18
```

**Output:**

```text
index  close  closes
0      9      [9]
1      12     [9,12]
2      12     [9,12,12]
3      15     [9,12,12,15]
4      12     [9,12,12,15,12]
5      18     [9,12,12,15,12,18]
```

**See also:** [`array.pop`](#array.pop)

entries.summary: Removes the last element of an array and returns it.

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The array to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.returns: The removed element.
entries.body:
An empty array stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `pop` returns the last element, 30, and leaves the other two.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
removed = values.pop()
emit "removed" removed
emit "values" values
```

**Output:**

```text
index  removed  values
0      30       [10,20]
```

**See also:** [`array.push`](#array.push)

entries.summary: Removes every element of an array.

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The array to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.body:
**Example:** After `clear`, `values` has no elements, so `size` is 0 and `empty` is `true`.

```tea
values = array.from(10, 20, 30)
values.clear()
emit "size" values.size()
emit "empty" values.is_empty()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  size  empty
0      0     true
```

**See also:** [`array.pop`](#array.pop)

entries.summary: Returns a copy of an array.
entries.returns: A new array with the same elements.
entries.body:
Arrays are values, so plain assignment already copies: after `b = a`, `b.push(x)` leaves `a` unchanged, and a function that pushes to an array it receives changes only its own copy. The copy is shallow: struct elements still refer to the same structs.

**Example:** Pushing to the copy `b` leaves `a` with its two elements.

```tea
a = array.from(1.0, 2.0)
b = a.copy()
b.push(3.0)
emit "a" a
emit "b" b
```

**Output:**

```text
index  a      b
0      [1,2]  [1,2,3]
```

pages.title: matrix
pages.description: Functions for two-dimensional collections.
pages.intro: See [types](#reference/language/types) for the `matrix<T>` type and [memory model](#memory-model) for how matrix values are copied and shared. Unlike Pine Script, where collections are references, a Tea collection is a value: assigning it or passing it to a function copies it, so a function that pushes to its argument leaves the caller’s collection unchanged. Every function whose first parameter is `self` can also be called as a method on the collection: `values.push(x)` is the same call as `array.push(values, x)`.

entries.summary: Creates a matrix with a fixed number of rows and columns.
signatures:
matrix<T> matrix.new<T: storable>(
    series int rows,
    series int columns,
    series T initial = …
)

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: The number of rows. Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The number of columns. Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: initial
parameters.description: The value of every element. Without it, every element is `na`, or `false` in a `matrix<bool>`.

entries.returns: A new matrix.
entries.body:
Without arguments the matrix has no rows or columns, and the element type must be written: `matrix.new<float>()`. A matrix keeps its shape; no function adds or removes rows or columns. A negative or `na` dimension stops the run with an error. A collection holds at most 100,000 elements; a larger matrix also stops the run. Each change copies the collection and counts against a per-bar allocation budget; see [`matrix.set`](#matrix.set). A `for … in` loop cannot iterate over a matrix; loop over its rows and columns by index.

**Example:** `grid` has 2 rows and 3 columns of zeros; after the `set`, its second row ends with 5.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<float>(2, 3, 0.0)
grid.set(1, 2, 5.0)
emit "rows" grid.rows()
emit "columns" grid.columns()
emit "second_row" grid.row(1)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  rows  columns  second_row
0      2     3        [0,0,5]
```

entries.summary: Returns the number of rows in a matrix.
entries.returns: The number of rows.

entries.summary: Returns the number of columns in a matrix.
entries.returns: The number of columns.

entries.summary: Returns the number of elements in a matrix.
entries.returns: The number of rows times the number of columns.

entries.summary: Returns the element at a row and column.
signatures:
T matrix.get<T: storable>(
    series matrix<T> self,
    series int row,
    series int column
)
entries.returns: The element. A struct element is the same struct, not a copy.
entries.body:
A row or column outside the matrix, or `na`, stops the run with an error.

**Example:** Rows and columns count from 0, so `grid.get(1, 0)` reads the first element of the second row, 7.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<int>(2, 2, 0)
grid.set(1, 0, 7)
emit "cell" grid.get(1, 0)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  cell
0      7
```

**See also:** [`matrix.set`](#matrix.set)

entries.summary: Replaces the element at a row and column.
signatures:
void matrix.set<T: storable>(
    series matrix<T> self,
    series int row,
    series int column,
    series T value
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The matrix to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.body:
A row or column outside the matrix, or `na`, stops the run with an error. A function that changes a matrix it receives changes only its own copy.

Each `set`, like every change to a collection, copies the whole collection into new storage. One bar may allocate at most 10,000 times and 16 MiB in all, where each copy counts 16 bytes plus 8 for each number, bool, string or color it holds; past either limit the run stops with `HEAP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. So a 100 by 100 matrix of numbers created in a bar allows 208 calls to `set` in that bar, and the 209th fails.

**Example:** `grid.set(0, 1, 7)` changes only the second element of the first row.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<int>(2, 2, 0)
grid.set(0, 1, 7)
emit "first_row" grid.row(0)
emit "second_row" grid.row(1)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  first_row  second_row
0      [0,7]      [0,0]
```

**See also:** [`matrix.get`](#matrix.get), [`matrix.fill`](#matrix.fill)

entries.summary: Sets every element of a matrix to one value.
signatures:
void matrix.fill<T: storable>(
    series matrix<T> self,
    series T value
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The matrix to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.body:
Each change copies the collection and counts against a per-bar allocation budget; see [`matrix.set`](#matrix.set).

**Example:** After `fill(1)`, every element of both rows is 1.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<int>(2, 2, 0)
grid.fill(1)
emit "first_row" grid.row(0)
emit "second_row" grid.row(1)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  first_row  second_row
0      [1,1]      [1,1]
```

**See also:** [`matrix.set`](#matrix.set)

entries.summary: Returns one row of a matrix as a new array.
signatures:
array<T> matrix.row<T: storable>(
    series matrix<T> self,
    series int row
)
entries.returns: A new array of the row’s elements from left to right; later changes to the matrix do not affect it.
entries.body:
A row outside the matrix, or `na`, stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `top` was read before the `set`, so it keeps the old first row; `changed` shows the 9.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<int>(2, 3, 0)
top = grid.row(0)
grid.set(0, 1, 9)
emit "top" top
emit "changed" grid.row(0)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  top      changed
0      [0,0,0]  [0,9,0]
```

**See also:** [`matrix.column`](#matrix.column)

entries.summary: Returns one column of a matrix as a new array.
signatures:
array<T> matrix.column<T: storable>(
    series matrix<T> self,
    series int column
)
entries.returns: A new array of the column’s elements from top to bottom; later changes to the matrix do not affect it.
entries.body:
A column outside the matrix, or `na`, stops the run with an error.

**Example:** The second column reads 7 from the first row and 0 from the second.

```tea
grid = matrix.new<int>(2, 3, 0)
grid.set(0, 1, 7)
emit "second_column" grid.column(1)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  second_column
0      [7,0]
```

**See also:** [`matrix.row`](#matrix.row)

entries.summary: Returns a copy of a matrix.
entries.returns: A new matrix with the same shape and elements.
entries.body:
Matrices are values, so plain assignment already copies them, and a function that changes a matrix it receives changes only its own copy. The copy is shallow: struct elements still refer to the same structs.

**Example:** Setting an element of the copy `b` leaves `a` unchanged.

```tea
a = matrix.new<int>(1, 2, 0)
b = a.copy()
b.set(0, 0, 5)
emit "a" a.row(0)
emit "b" b.row(0)
```

**Output:**

```text
index  a      b
0      [0,0]  [5,0]
```

pages.title: map
pages.description: Functions for key-value collections.
pages.intro: See [types](#reference/language/types) for the `map<K, V>` type and [memory model](#memory-model) for how map values are copied and shared. Unlike Pine Script, where collections are references, a Tea collection is a value: assigning it or passing it to a function copies it, so a function that pushes to its argument leaves the caller’s collection unchanged. Every function whose first parameter is `self` can also be called as a method on the collection: `values.push(x)` is the same call as `array.push(values, x)`.

entries.summary: Creates an empty map.
signatures: const map<K, V> map.new<K: map-key, V: storable>()
entries.returns: A new map with no entries.
entries.body:
Write the key and value types in angle brackets, as in `map.new<string, float>()`. Keys can be `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, `color` or an enum, and an `na` key stops the run with an error. A map keeps its keys in the order they were added. A collection holds at most 100,000 elements. Each change copies the collection and counts against a per-bar allocation budget; see [`map.put`](#map.put). A variable declared as `map<string, float> prices = na` holds no map, and calling a function on it stops the run with an error.

**Example:** `latest` holds only the key `"close"`, so looking up `"open"` gives `na`.

```tea
latest = map.new<string, float>()
latest.put("close", close)
emit "close" latest.get("close")
emit "open" latest.get("open")
```

```csv
time,close
0,9
1,12
2,12
3,15
4,12
5,18
```

**Output:**

```text
index  close  open
0      9      na
1      12     na
2      12     na
3      15     na
4      12     na
5      18     na
```

**See also:** [`map.put`](#map.put), [`map.get`](#map.get)

entries.summary: Returns the number of entries in a map.
signatures: int map.size<K: map-key, V: storable>(series map<K, V> self)
entries.returns: The number of keys.

entries.summary: Tests whether a map has no entries.
entries.returns: `true` when the map has no keys.

entries.summary: Tests whether a map has a key.
signatures:
bool map.contains<K: map-key, V: storable>(
    series map<K, V> self,
    series K key
)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to look for. Cannot be `na`.

entries.returns: `true` when the key is present, even if its value is `na`.
entries.body:
**Example:** The key `"gap"` is present although its value is `na`, so `stored` is `true` while `value` is `na`.

```tea
levels = map.new<string, float>()
levels.put("gap", na)
emit "stored" levels.contains("gap")
emit "value" levels.get("gap")
```

**Output:**

```text
index  stored  value
0      true    na
```

**See also:** [`map.get`](#map.get)

entries.summary: Returns the value stored under a key.
signatures:
V map.get<K: map-key, V: storable>(
    series map<K, V> self,
    series K key
)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to look up. Cannot be `na`.

entries.returns: The value, or the value type’s empty value (`na`, or `false` for `bool`) when the key is absent. Use [`map.contains`](#map.contains) to tell an absent key from a stored `na`.
entries.body:
Keys match by value; colors match by their channels, so `#FF0000` and `#FF0000FF` are the same key.

**Example:** `"z"` is not a key, so `missing` is `na` and `has_z` is `false`.

```tea
levels = map.new<string, float>()
levels.put("a", 1.5)
emit "a" levels.get("a")
emit "missing" levels.get("z")
emit "has_z" levels.contains("z")
```

**Output:**

```text
index  a    missing  has_z
0      1.5  na       false
```

**See also:** [`map.contains`](#map.contains), [`map.put`](#map.put)

entries.summary: Stores a value under a key, replacing any value already there.
signatures:
void map.put<K: map-key, V: storable>(
    series map<K, V> self,
    series K key,
    series V value
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The map to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to store under. Cannot be `na`.

entries.body:
Replacing a value keeps its key’s position; a new key goes last. A collection holds at most 100,000 elements; adding a key past that stops the run with an error. A function that puts into a map it receives changes only its own copy.

Each `put`, like every change to a collection, copies the whole collection into new storage. One bar may allocate at most 10,000 times and 16 MiB in all, where each copy counts 16 bytes plus 8 for each number, bool, string or color it holds; past either limit the run stops with `HEAP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. So a map from strings to numbers created empty in a bar fails on its 1,447th new key in that bar.

**Example:** Replacing the value under `"b"` keeps `"b"` first; `"a"`, added after it, stays second.

```tea
counts = map.new<string, int>()
counts.put("b", 1)
counts.put("a", 2)
counts.put("b", 3)
emit "keys" counts.keys()
emit "values" counts.values()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  keys       values
0      ["b","a"]  [3,2]
```

**See also:** [`map.get`](#map.get), [`map.remove`](#map.remove)

entries.summary: Removes a key from a map and returns its value.
signatures:
V map.remove<K: map-key, V: storable>(
    series map<K, V> self,
    series K key
)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The map to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to remove. Cannot be `na`.

entries.returns: The removed value, or the value type’s empty value (`na`, or `false` for `bool`) when the key was absent.
entries.body:
A key that is added again after removal goes last.

**Example:** Removing `"b"` returns its value, 1; put back, `"b"` now comes after `"a"`.

```tea
counts = map.new<string, int>()
counts.put("b", 1)
counts.put("a", 2)
removed = counts.remove("b")
counts.put("b", 3)
emit "removed" removed
emit "keys" counts.keys()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  removed  keys
0      1        ["a","b"]
```

**See also:** [`map.put`](#map.put)

entries.summary: Removes every entry of a map.
signatures: void map.clear<K: map-key, V: storable>(series map<K, V> self)

parameters.name: self
parameters.description: The map to update. Must be a variable or field; the call updates it.

entries.summary: Returns the keys of a map as a new array.
entries.returns: A new array of the keys, in the order they were added.
entries.body: **See also:** [`map.values`](#map.values)

entries.summary: Returns the values of a map as a new array.
entries.returns: A new array of the values, in the order their keys were added.
entries.body: **See also:** [`map.keys`](#map.keys)

entries.summary: Returns a copy of a map.
entries.returns: A new map with the same entries in the same order.
entries.body:
Maps are values, so plain assignment already copies them, and a function that changes a map it receives changes only its own copy. The copy is shallow: struct values still refer to the same structs.

**Example:** Adding a key to the copy `b` leaves `a` with its one key.

```tea
a = map.new<string, int>()
a.put("x", 1)
b = a.copy()
b.put("y", 2)
emit "a" a.keys()
emit "b" b.keys()
```

**Output:**

```text
index  a      b
0      ["x"]  ["x","y"]
```

pages.title: trade
pages.description: Trade coordinators that send a strategy's orders to a broker and record every fill in a portfolio, plus helpers that size entries and set rebalance targets.
pages.intro:
Trade coordinators that send a strategy's orders to a broker and record every fill in a portfolio, plus helpers that size entries and set rebalance targets.

Add `import trade` together with `import broker` and `import portfolio`. A
coordinator owns one broker value and one portfolio value. It submits orders
to the broker and applies each fill to the portfolio before the broker
matches anything else, so later checks see the new cash and position. The
four coordinators, made by [`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen), [`trade.ohlc`](#trade.ohlc),
[`trade.path`](#trade.path) and [`trade.lots`](#trade.lots), differ in when and at what price
orders fill, and [`trade.lots`](#trade.lots) keeps each entry as a separate lot;
Strategies compares them.

A complete strategy that uses all three libraries:

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(fast, slow)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(fast, slow)

// `var` keeps the coordinator, its orders and its books from bar to bar.
var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(commission = broker.commissionPercent(0.1)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if crossedUp and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
if crossedDown and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)

metrics = strat.snapshot()
plot("equity", metrics.equity)
plot("max drawdown", metrics.maxDrawdown)
```

Add `import trade` to a script to use these as `trade.name`.

entries.summary: Sizes an entry as a percentage of the portfolio's equity, read when `entry` is called.
signatures:
trade.percentOfEquity(
    float percent,
    bool commissionIncluded = false
)

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Percentage of equity, above `0` and at most `100`.

parameters.name: commissionIncluded
parameters.description: Whether the budget also pays the commission.

entries.returns: `trade.Sizing`: sizing for the `sizing` argument of `entry`.
entries.body:
The equity is the one from the latest `mark` or `end_bar`, or the initial
cash before the first. When the order fills, the budget is divided by the
execution price, the matched price after adverse slippage. With
`commissionIncluded`, the commission comes out of the budget; otherwise it is
charged on top.

The broker checks capital when the order fills, unless the portfolio's margin
for the order's side is `0`. The capital is the cash for a buy and the equity
at the matched price for a sell. With the commission on top, a buy needs
`notional * marginLong / 100 + fee <= cash` and a sell
`notional * marginShort / 100 + fee <= equity`; with the commission included,
the budget must be at most the capital. So with a commission above `0` and a
margin of `100`, the default of [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new),
`percentOfEquity(100)` is rejected whenever the marked equity is at least
the capital, as on a flat account with no fill since the last mark. A
`percent` of `0` or less, above `100` or `na`, or marked equity that is not
positive, makes the broker reject the order with `invalidQuantity` when it
would fill.

In the formula, B is the budget, E the marked equity, q the quantity, x the
execution price, c the commission setting, f the commission on the fill, m
the margin for the order's side and A the capital. The opening fill of a
reversal pays no per-order commission, as the closing fill already did.

**Formula**

$$
\begin{aligned}
B &= \frac{\mathit{percent}}{100} \cdot E \\
q &= \begin{cases}
B / x & \text{commission on top} \\
B / \bigl(x\,(1 + c)\bigr) & \text{included, commission rate } c \\
B / (x + c) & \text{included, } c \text{ per contract} \\
(B - c) / x & \text{included, } c \text{ per order}
\end{cases} \\
\text{fills only if } & m = 0 \text{ or } \begin{cases}
q\,x\,m / 100 + f \le A & \text{commission on top} \\
B \le A & \text{included}
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Example:** Three coordinators send the same buy on bar 0. One tick of slippage turns bar
1's open of 99 into an execution price of 100, and each order pays a
commission of 5. Half of the 1000 equity buys 500 / 100 = 5 units with the
commission on top, or (500 - 5) / 100 = 4.95 with it included. The 100% order
is rejected: 1000 of notional plus 5 of commission is more than the cash.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fees = broker.commissionCashPerOrder(5.0)
slip = broker.slippageTicks(1.0, 1.0)
var onTop = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(commission = fees, slippage = slip),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
var included = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(commission = fees, slippage = slip),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
var whole = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(commission = fees, slippage = slip),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
onTop.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
included.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
whole.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    onTop.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
    included.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0, true))
    whole.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(100.0))
onTop.end_bar(close, false)
included.end_bar(close, false)
whole.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "on top qty" onTop.position_quantity()
emit "on top cash" onTop.cash()
emit "included qty" included.position_quantity()
emit "included cash" included.cash()
emit "100% qty" whole.position_quantity()
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,99,99
1,99,100
2,100,101
3,101,102
```

**Output:**

```text
index  open  on top qty  on top cash  included qty  included cash  100% qty
0      99    0           1000         0             1000           0
1      99    5           495          4.95          500            0
2      100   5           495          4.95          500            0
3      101   5           495          4.95          500            0
```

**See also:** [`trade.percentOfEquityAtFill`](#trade.percentOfEquityAtFill), [`broker.Commission`](#broker.Commission)

entries.summary: Sizes an entry as a percentage of the equity at the moment the order fills.
signatures:
trade.percentOfEquityAtFill(
    float percent,
    bool commissionIncluded = false
)

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Percentage of equity, above `0` and at most `100`.

parameters.name: commissionIncluded
parameters.description: Whether the budget also pays the commission.

entries.returns: `trade.Sizing`: sizing for the `sizing` argument of `entry`.
entries.body:
The broker values equity as cash plus the position at the matched price,
before slippage; for the opening fill of a reversal, that is after the
closing fill, with no position left. The quantity is the budget divided by
the execution price, the matched price after adverse slippage, once an
included commission is taken out, and the capital check of
[`trade.percentOfEquity`](#trade.percentOfEquity) applies. When the order would fill, the broker
rejects it with `invalidQuantity` for a `percent` of `0` or less, above
`100` or `na`, and with `invalidAccountState` when that equity is not
positive.

In the formula, Q is the position just before the fill, r the matched price,
B the budget, q the quantity, x the execution price and c the commission
setting. The opening fill of a reversal pays no per-order commission, as the
closing fill already did.

**Formula**

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \mathit{cash} + Q \cdot r \\
B &= \frac{\mathit{percent}}{100} \cdot E \\
q &= \begin{cases}
B / x & \text{commission on top} \\
B / \bigl(x\,(1 + c)\bigr) & \text{included, commission rate } c \\
B / (x + c) & \text{included, } c \text{ per contract} \\
(B - c) / x & \text{included, } c \text{ per order}
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Example:** The short entry sent on bar 2 reverses the long at bar 3's open of 125.
Selling the 5 units leaves 1125 of cash and no position, so 50% of equity at
the fill is 562.5, which sells 562.5 / 125 = 4.5 units short.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.entry("Short", trade.Direction.short,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquityAtFill(50.0))
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,100,100
1,100,110
2,110,120
3,125,125
```

**Output:**

```text
index  open  fill qty  position  cash
0      100   na        0         1000
1      100   5         5         500
2      110   na        5         500
3      125   4.5       -4.5      1687.5
```

**See also:** [`trade.percentOfEquity`](#trade.percentOfEquity)

entries.summary: Creates a rebalance target for an exact signed position size.

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: Target position: positive for long, negative for short, `0` for flat.

entries.returns: `broker.PositionTarget`: a target for a coordinator's `rebalance`.
entries.body:
When the rebalance fills, the broker trades the difference between `quantity`
and the position at that moment, at the execution price, and cancels the
order when the difference is at most 0.0000001. The result is not always
exact. Unless the portfolio's `marginLong` is `0`, a buy from a flat or long
position is capped, without a rejection, at the quantity whose notional plus
commission spends the cash; when the cash buys nothing, the broker rejects
the order with `invalidAccountState`. A sell that opens or adds to a short,
and a fill that crosses zero, must pass a capital check unless the
portfolio's margin for the new side is `0`, or the broker rejects it with
`invalidAccountState`: the opened quantity times the execution price, plus
the fee, plus, when crossing zero, the slippage paid on closing the old
position, must be at most the equity at the matched price.

In the formula, Q is the position before the fill, q the quantity traded, x
the execution price and c the commission setting.

**Formula**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &= \mathit{quantity} - Q \\
q &= \begin{cases}
\min\bigl(|\Delta|,\ \max(0,\ q_{\text{cash}})\bigr)
  & \Delta > 0,\ Q \ge 0,\ \mathit{marginLong} \ne 0 \\
|\Delta| & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases} \\
q_{\text{cash}} &= \begin{cases}
\mathit{cash} / \bigl(x\,(1 + c)\bigr) & \text{commission rate } c \\
\mathit{cash} / (x + c) & c \text{ per contract} \\
(\mathit{cash} - c) / x & c \text{ per order}
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Example:** A target of 1000 units fills only 10 at bar 1, because the 1000 of cash buys
no more; no rejection is reported. A target of 4 then sells 6. The same
target again needs no change, so bar 3 cancels it without a fill.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(1000.0))
if bar_index == 1 or bar_index == 2
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(4.0))
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
emit "pending" strat.has_pending() ? 1 : 0
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,100,100
1,100,100
2,100,100
3,100,100
```

**Output:**

```text
index  fill qty  position  cash  pending
0      na        0         1000  1
1      10        10        0     1
2      6         4         600   1
3      na        4         600   0
```

**See also:** [`trade.targetPercentOfEquity`](#trade.targetPercentOfEquity), [`trade.NextOpenTrade.rebalance`](#trade.NextOpenTrade.rebalance)

entries.summary: Creates a rebalance target worth a signed percentage of equity when the order fills.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Target position value as a percentage of equity, from `-100` to `100`; negative means short.

entries.returns: `broker.PositionTarget`: a target for a coordinator's `rebalance`.
entries.body:
When the rebalance fills, the broker values equity at the matched price,
before slippage, converts the percentage to a quantity at that same price,
and trades the difference as [`trade.targetQuantity`](#trade.targetQuantity) does, including its
cap on buys. The fill pays the execution price, so with a slippage rate s a
buy from flat costs (1 + s) times the target value: a 50% target with 1%
slippage costs 50.5% of equity. A percentage beyond `100` in either direction
makes `rebalance` return `na`, and the broker rejects the order with
`invalidAccountState` when the matched price or the equity is not positive.

In the formula, Q is the position before the fill, r the matched price and T
the target quantity.

**Formula**

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \mathit{cash} + Q \cdot r \\
T &= \frac{\mathit{percent}}{100} \cdot \frac{E}{r} \\
\Delta &= T - Q
\end{aligned}
$$

**Example:** With 1% slippage, a 50% target of the 1000 equity is converted at bar 1's
open of 100 into 5 units, which fill at 101 and cost 505, 50.5% of equity.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(slippage = broker.slippagePercent(1.0)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.rebalance("Half", trade.targetPercentOfEquity(50.0))
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "fill price" na(filled) ? na : filled.price
emit "cost" na(filled) ? na : filled.notional
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,100,100
1,100,100
2,100,100
3,100,100
```

**Output:**

```text
index  open  fill qty  fill price  cost
0      100   na        na          na
1      100   5         101         505
2      100   na        na          na
3      100   na        na          na
```

**See also:** [`trade.targetQuantity`](#trade.targetQuantity), [`trade.NextOpenTrade.rebalance`](#trade.NextOpenTrade.rebalance)

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator whose orders fill at a later bar's open, or at a bar's close when the broker processes orders on close.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.NextOpenBroker`](#broker.NextOpenBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: `trade.NextOpenTrade`: a coordinator that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, bar_index)` before the signal logic and
`end_bar(close, false)` after it. With a broker created with
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, `end_bar` also fills orders at the close,
including orders submitted earlier in the same bar. A broker or portfolio
without the required methods is a compile error.

**Example:** A close above the highest of the three previous closes buys with 50% of
equity, and a close below the lowest of them sells. With
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, each order fills at the close of the bar that
sends it: the buy of 500 / 125 = 4 units at bar 3's close of 125, and the
sale at bar 6's close of 110.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

highest = ta.highest(close, 3)
lowest = ta.lowest(close, 3)
var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(processOrdersOnClose = true),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if close > highest[1] and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Breakout", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
if close < lowest[1] and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Breakdown")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "close" close
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "equity" strat.snapshot().equity
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,100,100
1,100,102
2,102,101
3,101,125
4,125,130
5,130,120
6,120,110
7,110,105
```

**Output:**

```text
index  close  position  equity
0      100    0         1000
1      102    0         1000
2      101    0         1000
3      125    4         1000
4      130    4         1020
5      120    4         980
6      110    0         940
7      105    0         940
```

**See also:** [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade)

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that matches orders and one stop-loss and/or take-profit exit against each bar's open, high and low.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.OhlcBroker`](#broker.OhlcBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: `trade.OhlcTrade`: a coordinator that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)`, submit orders and
exits, then call `end_bar(close, false)`. [`trade.path`](#trade.path) replays the bar
as an ordered path instead and has trailing exits. A broker or portfolio
without the required methods is a compile error.

**Example:** From bar 2, a buy stop sits at the highest high of the last three bars, 125,
with an exit 5% below and 10% above it. Bar 3's high reaches 125 and buys 50%
of the 1000 equity, 4 units. Bar 5's high reaches the target of 137.5, which
sells them for a gain of 50.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

upper = ta.highest(high, 3)
var strat = trade.ohlc(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
matches = strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)
if strat.position_quantity() == 0.0 and not na(upper)
    // The same ids move the pending stop entry and its exit each bar.
    strat.entry("Breakout", trade.Direction.long, stop = upper,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
    strat.exit("Bracket", fromEntry = "Breakout", stop = upper * 0.95,
        target = upper * 1.1)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "high" high
emit "entry" na(matches.pending) ? na : matches.pending.price
emit "exit" na(matches.exit) ? na : matches.exit.price
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "equity" strat.snapshot().equity
```

```csv
time,open,high,low,close
0,120,125,119,124
1,124,124,121,122
2,122,123,120,121
3,121,128,120,127
4,127,132,126,131
5,131,139,130,138
6,138,138,134,135
```

**Output:**

```text
index  high  entry  exit   position  equity
0      125   na     na     0         1000
1      124   na     na     0         1000
2      123   na     na     0         1000
3      128   125    na     4         1008
4      132   na     na     4         1024
5      139   na     137.5  0         1050
6      138   na     na     0         1050
```

**See also:** [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade)

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that replays each bar as an ordered price path, with fixed and trailing exits.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.PathBroker`](#broker.PathBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: `trade.PathTrade`: a coordinator that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)`, attach or
adjust exits, call `continue_bar(open, high, low, close)`, submit new orders,
then call `end_bar(close, false)`. A broker or portfolio without the required
methods is a compile error.

**Example:** The 2-bar average crosses above the 3-bar average on bar 3, and the entry
buys 50% of the 1000 equity, 5 units, at bar 4's open of 100. The exit
attached from that fill has a stop at 95 and a trailing stop that starts at
105 and keeps 2 below the best price. Bar 4's path rises to 112, which puts
the trailing stop at 110, and bar 5's path falls through it.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

crossedUp = ta.crossover(ta.sma(close, 2), ta.sma(close, 3))
var strat = trade.path(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
matches = strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)
if not na(matches.pending) and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    // Levels from the fill; continue_bar checks the rest of this bar.
    price = matches.pending.price
    strat.exit("Trail", fromEntry = "Long", stop = price * 0.95,
        activateOnEntryBar = true, trailPrice = price * 1.05,
        trailOffset = price * 0.02)
exitFill = strat.continue_bar(open, high, low, close)
if crossedUp and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "close" close
emit "entry" na(matches.pending) ? na : matches.pending.price
emit "exit" na(exitFill) ? na : exitFill.price
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that opens and closes separately accounted lots at once, within the current bar.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.ImmediateBroker`](#broker.ImmediateBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.LotLedger`](#portfolio.LotLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.lots`](#portfolio.lots).

entries.returns: `trade.LotTrade`: a coordinator that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(close, bar_index)`, then `entry`, `close_trade` or
`close_trade_at_stop`, then `mark()`. Each entry fill carries the `tradeId`
that later closes name. A broker or portfolio without the required methods is
a compile error.

**Example:** The close crosses above its 3-bar average on bar 3, and lot 1 buys 500 of
notional, 5 units, at the close of 100, with a stop 3% below at 97. Bar 4's
low reaches the stop, which closes the lot at 97. Lot 2 opens at the next
cross, on bar 5, and closes at bar 7's close of 101, when the close crosses
back under the average.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

basis = ta.sma(close, 3)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(close, basis)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(close, basis)
var strat = trade.lots(broker.new(),
    portfolio.lots(initialCash = 1000.0))
var int lot = 0
var float lotStop = na
strat.begin_bar(close, bar_index)
if lot > 0
    stopFill = strat.close_trade_at_stop("Stop", lot, broker.Side.buy, open,
        high, low, lotStop)
    if not na(stopFill)
        lot := 0
if lot > 0 and crossedDown
    strat.close_trade("Exit", lot)
    lot := 0
if lot == 0 and crossedUp
    entryFill = strat.entry("Long", "Cover", trade.Direction.long,
        notional = 500.0)
    if not na(entryFill)
        lot := entryFill.tradeId
        lotStop := close * 0.97
strat.mark()
emit "close" close
emit "lot" lot
emit "cash" strat.cash()
emit "equity" strat.snapshot().equity
```

entries.summary: Side of a new position: long or short.

rows: A long position, opened by buying.
A short position, opened by selling.

entries.body:
A coordinator's `entry` buys for `long` and sells for `short`. A short sale
adds its proceeds to cash, and equity is cash plus the signed position times
the mark price, so a short loses equity as the price rises.

**Example:** Two coordinators enter 5 units at bar 1's open of 100, one long and one
short. The short sale adds 500 to cash, and the short's equity falls as the
close rises: 980 at 104 and 950 at 110.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var buyer = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
var seller = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
buyer.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
seller.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    buyer.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
    seller.entry("Short", trade.Direction.short, qty = 5.0)
buyer.end_bar(close, false)
seller.end_bar(close, false)
emit "close" close
emit "long equity" buyer.snapshot().equity
emit "short position" seller.position_quantity()
emit "short cash" seller.cash()
emit "short equity" seller.snapshot().equity
```

entries.summary: Which equity a [`trade.Sizing`](#trade.Sizing) percentage is taken from: the marked equity when `entry` is called, or the equity when the order fills.

rows: Equity from the latest `mark` or `end_bar`, read when `entry` is called.
Equity at the order's matched price before slippage, computed when the order fills.

entries.body:
**Example:** Both coordinators hold 5 units bought at 100 and add 12% of equity with an
order sent on bar 2. `percentOfEquity` takes the equity marked at bar 1's
close, 1200, and buys 144 / 150 = 0.96 units at bar 3's open of 150.
`percentOfEquityAtFill` takes the equity at that open, 1250, and buys 1.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var byMark = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0, pyramiding = 2))
var atFill = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0, pyramiding = 2))
a = byMark.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
b = atFill.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    byMark.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
    atFill.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    byMark.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(12.0))
    atFill.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquityAtFill(12.0))
byMark.end_bar(close, false)
atFill.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "close" close
emit "percentOfEquity" na(a) ? na : a.quantity
emit "percentOfEquityAtFill" na(b) ? na : b.quantity
```

entries.summary: Percent-of-equity sizing for an entry, made by [`trade.percentOfEquity`](#trade.percentOfEquity) or [`trade.percentOfEquityAtFill`](#trade.percentOfEquityAtFill).

rows: Which equity the percentage is taken from.
Value of the order as a percentage of equity; valid values are above `0` and at most `100`.
Whether the budget also pays the commission; when `false`, the commission is charged on top.

entries.body:
Pass it as the `sizing` argument of `entry` on [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade),
[`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade) or [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade). Nothing is checked when
it is made: if `value` is `0` or less, above `100` or `na`, the broker
rejects the order with `invalidQuantity` when it would fill.

**Example:** The helpers only fill in the fields, even with an out-of-range 150.

```tea
import trade

marked = trade.percentOfEquity(25.0)
atFill = trade.percentOfEquityAtFill(150.0, true)
emit "marked value" marked.value
emit "marked included" marked.commissionIncluded ? 1 : 0
emit "at fill value" atFill.value
emit "at fill included" atFill.commissionIncluded ? 1 : 0
atFillKind = atFill.kind == trade.SizingKind.percentOfEquityAtFill
emit "at fill kind" atFillKind ? 1 : 0
```

entries.summary: Coordinator whose orders fill at a later bar's open, or at a bar's close when the broker processes orders on close.

rows: Broker that validates and fills this coordinator's orders.
Portfolio that records this coordinator's fills.
Bar index from the latest `begin_bar`, or `-1` before the first; orders submitted later in the bar record it as their `signalBarIndex`.

entries.body:
Create it with [`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen). Each bar, call `begin_bar` before the
signal logic, submit orders, then call `end_bar`. An order fills at the open
of a bar after the one it was submitted on. With a broker created with
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, it can also fill at a close, including the
close of its own bar. The broker holds one pending order at a time and makes
at most two fills per bar; this family has no stop entries and no attached
exits. Strategies call these methods rather than the broker's or the
portfolio's own.

**Example:** The entry sent on bar 0 fills at bar 1's open of 100, and the close sent on
bar 2 fills at bar 3's open of 120. Equity is marked at each close.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "close" close
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
emit "equity" strat.snapshot().equity
```

entries.summary: Starts a bar: fills the pending order at `openPrice` and applies the fill to the portfolio.
entries.returns: `broker.Fill`: the last fill applied, which for a reversal is the opening fill, or `na` when nothing filled.
entries.body:
Call it once per bar, before the signal logic. An order can fill here
from the bar after it was submitted, so orders submitted later in this
bar wait. An entry against the open position fills twice at this open:
once to close the position, then once to open the new side. A reversal
whose opening fill did not fit in an earlier bar's two fills completes
here.

**Example:** The entry sent on bar 0 fills at bar 1's open. The short entry sent on
bar 2 reverses the position at bar 3's open: it sells the 5 units, then 2
more to open the short, and `begin_bar` returns that last fill.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.entry("Short", trade.Direction.short, qty = 2.0)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "fill price" na(filled) ? na : filled.price
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```

entries.summary: Submits an entry order that opens, adds to or reverses the position at a later bar's open, or at a close when the broker processes orders on close.
signatures:
broker.Order entry(
    string commandId,
    trade.Direction direction,
    float qty = na,
    trade.Sizing sizing = na
)

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: Name of the order; `cancel` takes it, and later entries that add to the position reuse it.

parameters.name: qty
parameters.description: Quantity to open or add; must be positive.

entries.returns: `broker.Order`: the accepted order, or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission.
entries.body:
Give at most one of `qty` and `sizing`. With neither, the entry spends
all available capital, commission included: the cash for a buy, the
equity for a sell. The quantity is `qty`, or the sizing budget divided by
the execution price, the matched price after adverse slippage, once any
commission the sizing includes is taken out ([`trade.percentOfEquity`](#trade.percentOfEquity)
gives the formula).

An entry against the open position reverses it with two fills: the first
closes the whole position, and the second opens the new side at the same
price, or at the next open when the first was the bar's second fill. An
entry without a size, or sized with [`trade.percentOfEquityAtFill`](#trade.percentOfEquityAtFill),
is sized from the account after the first fill, and a per-order
commission is charged on the first fill only. If the second fill is
rejected, the position is left flat. An entry on the position's side adds
to it only under the `commandId` of the entry that opened it, and only
while the position has fewer entries than the portfolio's `pyramiding`.

On submission the broker checks only the pending order and the id: the
method returns `na` when another order is pending, or when an entry on
the position's side uses another `commandId` (`entryIdMismatch`). The
rest is checked when the order would fill, and a rejection then shows
only as a [`broker.OrderRejected`](#broker.OrderRejected) event:

- `invalidQuantity` for both `qty` and `sizing`, a `qty` that is not
  positive, or invalid sizing;
- `invalidAccountState` for an add with no room under `pyramiding`, or
  for too little capital. Unless the portfolio's margin for the order's
  side is `0`, an order with `qty` or `sizing` needs
  `notional * marginLong / 100 + fee <= cash` for a buy and
  `notional * marginShort / 100 + fee <= equity` for a sell, with equity
  valued at the matched price; with the commission included in percent
  sizing, the budget must fit instead. An order with neither needs
  capital above `0`.

**Example:** On bar 0 the first entry is accepted as order 1, and the second returns
`na` because the first is pending. The first buys 50% of the 1000 equity,
500 / 100 = 5 units, at bar 1's open. The short entry sent on bar 2,
without a size, reverses at bar 3's open of 125: it sells the 5 units,
then sells short the whole equity of 1125, 9 units.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
int firstId = na
int secondId = na
if bar_index == 0
    first = strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long,
        sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
    second = strat.entry("Other", trade.Direction.long, qty = 1.0)
    firstId := na(first) ? na : first.id
    secondId := na(second) ? na : second.id
if bar_index == 2
    strat.entry("Short", trade.Direction.short)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "first id" firstId
emit "second id" secondId
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```


entries.summary: Submits an order that closes the whole position at a later bar's open, or at a close when the broker processes orders on close.

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: Name of the order; `cancel` takes it.

entries.returns: `broker.Order`: the accepted order, or `na` when another order is pending.
entries.body:
It closes whatever position is open when it fills. It returns `na` when
another order is pending; if the position is flat when it would fill, the
broker rejects it with `invalidAccountState`.

**Example:** The close sent on bar 2 sells all 5 units at bar 3's open of 120 and
realizes 5 * (120 - 100) = 100.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
emit "realized" strat.snapshot().realizedPnl
```

entries.summary: Submits an order that moves the position to a target size at a later bar's open, or at a close when the broker processes orders on close.
signatures:
broker.Order rebalance(
    string commandId,
    broker.PositionTarget target
)

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: Name of the order; `cancel` takes it.

entries.returns: `broker.Order`: the accepted order, or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission.
entries.body:
When it fills, the broker trades the difference between the target and
the position at that moment, in one fill even when the target is on the
other side of zero, and cancels the order when the difference is at most
0.0000001. Submitting again under the same `commandId` while the order is
pending replaces the target. It returns `na` when another order is
pending, when the target or its value is `na`, or when a percent target
is beyond `100` in either direction.

The position can stop short of the target. Unless the portfolio's
`marginLong` is `0`, a buy from a flat or long position is cut, without a
rejection, to the quantity whose notional plus commission spends the
cash. A sell that opens or adds to a short, and a fill that crosses zero,
must pass a capital check, or the broker rejects it with
`invalidAccountState`; [`trade.targetQuantity`](#trade.targetQuantity) gives the rules.

`pyramiding` never limits a rebalance. A rebalance that opens or reverses
the position counts as its first entry, and its `commandId` becomes the
position's entry id, so a later `entry` on that side must use that id or
returns `na` (`entryIdMismatch`). A rebalance that adds to or reduces the
position leaves the entry id and the entry count unchanged, and one that
closes it clears them.

**Example:** Bar 1 buys the 4 units of the first target. The target of 20 needs 16
more, but the 600 of cash buys only 6, so bar 2 stops at 10 units without
a rejection. The target of -2 sells 12 units in one fill at bar 3's open.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
filled = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(4.0))
if bar_index == 1
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(20.0))
if bar_index == 2
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(-2.0))
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "open" open
emit "fill qty" na(filled) ? na : filled.quantity
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
```

```csv
time,open,close
0,100,100
1,100,100
2,100,100
3,120,120
```

**Output:**

```text
index  open  fill qty  position  cash
0      100   na        0         1000
1      100   4         4         600
2      100   6         10        0
3      120   12        -2        1440
```

**Example:** The rebalance opens the position at bar 1, counts as its first entry and
gives it the id `Target`. An entry named `Long` then returns `na`; one
named `Target` is accepted and adds the second entry that
`pyramiding = 2` allows.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0, pyramiding = 2))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
int accepted = na
if bar_index == 0
    strat.rebalance("Target", trade.targetQuantity(5.0))
if bar_index == 1
    order = strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 1.0)
    accepted := na(order) ? 0 : 1
if bar_index == 2
    order = strat.entry("Target", trade.Direction.long, qty = 1.0)
    accepted := na(order) ? 0 : 1
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "accepted" accepted
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "entries" strat.snapshot().openTradeCount
```


```text
1      0         5         1
2      1         5         1
3      na        6         2
```

entries.summary: Cancels the pending order named `commandId`.

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: Name the order was submitted with.

entries.returns: `int`: `1` when the pending order had that name, otherwise `0`.
entries.body:
**Example:** No pending order is named `Short`, so that call returns 0. Cancelling
`Long` on bar 0 returns 1, and nothing fills at bar 1's open.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
int none = na
int cancelled = na
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
    none := strat.cancel("Short")
    cancelled := strat.cancel("Long")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "cancel Short" none
emit "cancel Long" cancelled
emit "pending" strat.has_pending() ? 1 : 0
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```

entries.summary: Fills the pending order at `closePrice` when the broker processes orders on close, and applies the fill.
entries.returns: `broker.Fill`: the last fill applied, or `na` when nothing filled.
entries.body:
Without `processOrdersOnClose = true` on the broker it fills nothing. Use
it with `mark` and `finish` in place of `end_bar` to act between those
steps: after one fill at the close, a new order submitted on the same bar
fills at the same close with a second call. A bar has at most two fills;
a third order waits for the next open, and so does the opening fill of a
reversal that would be the third.

**Example:** On bar 1, the entry fills at the close of 110, and a close sent next
fills at the same close: the bar's two fills. The third order waits and
fills at bar 2's open of 112.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(processOrdersOnClose = true),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
opened = strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
float first = na
float second = na
float third = na
if bar_index == 1
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
    a = strat.process_close(close)
    strat.close("Exit")
    b = strat.process_close(close)
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 2.0)
    c = strat.process_close(close)
    first := na(a) ? na : a.quantity
    second := na(b) ? na : b.quantity
    third := na(c) ? na : c.quantity
strat.mark(close)
emit "close" close
emit "first" first
emit "second" second
emit "third" third
emit "at open" na(opened) ? na : opened.quantity
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```

entries.summary: Values the portfolio at `price` and updates equity, peak equity and maximum drawdown.

parameters.name: price
parameters.description: Price to value the position at, normally [`close`](#close).

entries.returns: `float`: the new equity.
entries.body:
Equity is cash plus the signed position times `price`. `end_bar` marks at
the close; call `mark` directly when using `process_close` and `finish`
instead.

**Example:** The 5 units bought at 100 are valued at each close. Equity peaks at 1050
and falls to 950, a drawdown of 100 / 1050.

```tea

import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
equity = strat.mark(close)
emit "close" close
emit "equity" equity
emit "drawdown" strat.snapshot().maxDrawdown
```

entries.summary: On the last bar, expires the pending order without closing the position.

parameters.name: isLast
parameters.description: Whether this is the last bar of the data.

entries.returns: `broker.FinishResult`: the expired order in `pending`, or `na` when `isLast` is `false`.
entries.body:
Does nothing when `isLast` is `false`. Tea has no builtin that tells the
last bar, so the script has to know it, for example from an input.

**Example:** Bar 3 is the last bar. The close sent there can no longer fill, so
`finish` expires it, order 2, and the 5 units stay open.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
isLast = bar_index == 3
if bar_index == 0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if isLast
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.mark(close)
expired = strat.finish(isLast)
emit "expired" na(expired) ? na : expired.pending.id
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "pending" strat.has_pending() ? 1 : 0
```

```text
2      na       5         0
3      2        5         0
```

entries.summary: Ends the bar: runs `process_close`, `mark` and `finish` in that order.

parameters.name: isLast
parameters.description: Whether this is the last bar of the data.

entries.returns: `broker.FinishResult`: the orders expired on the last bar, or `na` when `isLast` is `false`.
entries.body:
With `processOrdersOnClose = true` on the broker, the pending order can
fill at `closePrice`, including one submitted on this bar. The portfolio
is then marked at `closePrice`, and on the last bar the pending order
expires. Tea has no builtin that tells the last bar, so pass `false`
unless the script knows it, for example from an input.

**Example:** With `processOrdersOnClose = true`, the entry sent on bar 1 fills at that
bar's close of 110 before equity is marked, and the close sent on bar 2
fills at 120.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(processOrdersOnClose = true),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 1000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if bar_index == 1
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
emit "close" close
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
emit "cash" strat.cash()
emit "equity" strat.snapshot().equity
```

entries.summary: Returns the average entry price of the open position, or `na` when flat.
entries.returns: `float`: the average entry price, or `na` when flat.
entries.body:
It is the quantity-weighted mean of the execution prices, after slippage,
of the fills that opened and added to the position; a fill that reduces
the position does not change it.

**Example:** With 1% slippage and `pyramiding = 2`, 5 units bought at 101 (open 100)
and 5 more at 111.1 (open 110) average 106.05. The close at bar 3 leaves

```tea
    broker.new(slippage = broker.slippagePercent(1.0)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 2000.0, pyramiding = 2))

if bar_index <= 1
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 5.0)
if bar_index == 2
    strat.close("Exit")

emit "open" open
emit "position" strat.position_quantity()
```
